In the context provided, Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, is a significant figure in Jewish history, leading the Jews back from Babylon around 520 BC, governing Judah, and rebuilding the temple. The Old Testament records several instances of him being called a son of Shealtiel.

In a different context, there is a reference to a forecasting model using a rolling origin method. This method involves making a forecast for the (k+i)th observation based on the observations from 1 to (k+i-1). The error on this forecast is then computed. This process is repeated for i = 2,...,T–k, where T is the total number of observations. The forecast accuracy is determined by aggregating all the errors computed. This procedure is often referred to as a "rolling forecasting origin" because the "origin" (k+i -1) at which the forecast is based moves forward in time.

Two-step-ahead or p-step-ahead forecasts can be computed by first making a forecast for the (k+i)th observation, then making a forecast for the (k+i+1)th observation using the updated origin (k+i) and so on, for p steps ahead. This process allows for a more extended look into the future based on the available data.
